item.title: South Carolina Basketball Suffers First Loss Of The Season In Thriller
item.description: Photo by: Jeff Blake South Carolina basketball came within a few possessions of pulling off an impressive upset Wednesday afternoon, but the Gamecocks ultimately fell 71-69 to No. 18 USC in the Acrisure Series in Palm Desert, California. The Gamecocks entered the matchup undefeated at 5-0 and faced their biggest challenge of the young season against a talented USC team. South Carolina controlled much of the contest, held a halftime lead and appeared to be in position to hand the Trojans their first loss. However, USC found a way to turn things around late, using a decisive run in the final minutes to escape with the victory. With the loss, South Carolina dropped to 5-1, while USC improved to 7-0 and kept its perfect record intact. Gamecocks Set the Tone Early South Carolina came out ready to compete, showing it was not intimidated by the nationally ranked Trojans. The Gamecocks used strong outside shooting to keep USC’s defense off balance. Camden Heide was especially effective from beyond the arc, knocking down four three pointers and finishing with 12 points. Aleksas Bieliauskas also delivered a major performance inside. The forward scored 18 points and grabbed 12 rebounds, giving South Carolina an important presence on both ends of the floor. The Gamecocks built an early advantage and continued making shots throughout the opening half. Their three-point shooting helped them stay ahead of USC’s high powered offense. South Carolina entered halftime with a 37-35 lead, putting itself in a strong position to compete for another important victory. South Carolina Holds Its Ground After Halftime The second half featured plenty of back and forth action, with South Carolina continuing to find ways to slow down the Trojans. USC entered the game averaging more than 94 points per contest, but the Gamecocks did a strong job limiting its offensive production. The Trojans struggled from the field and particularly had trouble finding their rhythm from three point range. Alijah Arenas became the biggest offensive weapon for USC. He finished with a game-high 25 points and consistently found opportunities to attack the basket and get to the free throw line. Rodney Rice added 13 points, although he struggled with his shooting and finished with five turnovers. South Carolina continued to lead for much of the afternoon and built a 10 point advantage with just over eight minutes remaining. At that point, the Gamecocks appeared to be closing in on a major upset. USC Delivers Late Comeback Unfortunately for South Carolina, the final minutes belonged to the Trojans. USC increased its defensive pressure and began taking advantage of opportunities at the free-throw line. The Trojans closed the game on a 10-2 run, holding the Gamecocks scoreless over the final 4:05. South Carolina had opportunities to regain the lead, but late missed shots prevented the Gamecocks from completing the upset. Arenas led the comeback and finished 12 of 13 from the free throw line. item.title: Detroit Lions vs. Chicago Bears preview: 4 key stats
item.description: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - SEPTEMBER 14: Brian Branch #32 of the Detroit Lions attempts to sack Caleb Williams #18 of the Chicago Bears during an NFL football game at Ford Field on September 14, 2025 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images The two most recent NFC North division champions pitted against each other to kick off the NFL’s Thanksgiving spectacular. Both teams are 8-2 in loaded divisional and conference races. Dan Campbell vs. Ben Johnson. This is why the NFL is undefeated. One of the few hurdles Campbell has yet to clear is finding consistent success on Turkey Day. After going 1-5 on Thanksgiving as a player with the Lions and Dallas Cowboys, Campbell is just 1-4 as the Lions’ head coach in their annual spotlight game. Detroit is 1-8 on Thanksgiving over the last nine seasons, with the Chicago Bears alone going 3-1 against the Lions in that span. The Lions have endured a grueling stretch, returning from Germany and playing last week without the luxury of a bye, followed by this short four-day turnaround. However, this game carries more weight than any they’ve played since their back-to-back divisional matchups against the Packers and Vikings. As a reminder, the Lions will play all three of their road divisional games over the last four games, making it even more imperative that they take care of business at home. This week’s Lions-Bears preview will focus on both sides of the ball, with a heightened emphasis on how defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard’s burgeoning defensive unit can turn Bears QB Caleb Williams into a turducken. Note: Unless otherwise indicated, all statistics are sourced from NFL Pro, FTN Fantasy, Pro Football Reference, SumerSports, or Pro Football Focus. Can’t Run Away From Your Problems The Bears’ offense this season hasn’t quite reached the heights of efficiency it attained at times last year, except Week 1, when it put together a 59-burger firework factory against the Panthers. In fact, while the Bears haven’t trailed since Williams returned to the lineup in Week 6, their offense has averaged just -0.04 EPA/play in that span, good for a clean league-average ranking of 16th. One area that’s had hiccups in that span is the run game, which has suffered from the downgrade of center Drew Dalman (offseason retirement) to Garrett Bradbury and the loss of tight end Cole Kmet to injured reserve, a rock-fighting Geodude on the perimeter. The Bears are still committed to running the football, with a 46.8% run rate (8th), but where they’re really struggling is on early downs, putting themselves behind the eight ball. Since Week 6, their 132 early-down (first- and second-down) rushing attempts have generated just 3.3 yards/rush (29th), -0.269 EPA/rush (32nd), and a 34.1% success rate (27th). That’s not the run-game wagon Ben Johnson, one of football’s better run-game architects, had rolling last year. item.title: James becomes oldest with NBA triple-double in Sixers win
item.description: LeBron James of the Philadelphia 76ers became the oldest NBA player to produce a triple double at barely a month before his 42nd birthday in a victory over the Miami Heat (Mitchell Leff) LeBron James became the oldest player in NBA history to produce a triple-double, leading Philadelphia to a 114-104 victory over Miami in the NBA Cup on Wednesday. Four-time NBA Most Valuable Player James, who turns 42 on December 30, scored a season-high 25 points, passed off a season-high 12 assists and pulled down 10 rebounds for the 76ers. Miami grabbed a 32-29 lead after the first quarter, but James scored 14 consecutive Sixers points in a second-quarter run for a 62-53 halftime lead, and the hosts never lost the lead in the second half. "We wanted to get back to our defensive identity," James said. "We didn't do that in the first quarter but for the next 36 minutes I thought we got back to that." The 76ers improved the best record in the Eastern Conference to 15-4 while snapping a seven-game win streak for Miami (10-7). Both clubs are 2-1 in East Group B Cup play, but with a win Miami would have clinched the group and advanced to the knockout stage of the in-season tournament. With Joel Embiid out due to illness and Jaylen Brown out after early left hamstring tightness, it fell to James to score and set up his teammates with NFL-ish passing. "That's my favorite aspect of my game besides my IQ," James said. "So to be able to go out there and just play like a quarterback role and watch these guys run the right routes and it's my job to put it on time and on target, it was fun." Tyrese Maxey led the 76ers with 30 points while fellow guard VJ Edgecombe added 18. "In this league you have to have some depth for sure," James said. "It's a fast-paced game. It feels good for us. These are my young bulls right here. They keep me going. They keep me energized." Greek star Giannis Antetokounmpo led Miami with 32 points and 14 rebounds. A late rebound gave James his first triple double with the 76ers, drawing a standing ovation from the Philadelphia crowd. James left the Los Angeles Lakers in the off-season and selected the 76ers from several clubs in hopes of capturing a fifth NBA crown. js/pnb

item.title: St. John’s faces daunting rebounding test against Louisville on Thanksgiving
item.description: St. John's Red Storm forward Ruben Prey (17) and Siena Saints guard Tim Ibukunoluwa (13) fight for a loose ball in Queens, N.Y., Wednesday, Nov. 18, 2026. LAS VEGAS — The top priority is pretty obvious for St. John’s on Thanksgiving night: rebounding, rebounding and more rebounding. Access the St. John's beat like never before Join Post Sports+ for exciting subscriber-only features, including real-time texting with Zach Braziller about the inside buzz on St. John’s. TRY IT NOW That was coach Rick Pitino’s biggest concern this week in Sin City, and the 13th-ranked Johnnies will have to deal with one of the best offensive rebounding teams in the country in No. 25 Louisville. Led by twin towers Flory Bidunga and Obinna Ekezie Jr., the Cardinals are seventh nationally in offensive rebounding percentage at 44.6. They hammered No. 5 Texas Tech on the glass, 41-28, in their Tuesday night opener of the Players Era Festival. “It’s a big focus for sure. They get [almost] 50 percent of their misses back,” Red Storm big man Ruben Prey said Wednesday. “We have to make that number lower.” Red Storm forward Ruben Prey (17) and Saints guard Tim Ibukunoluwa (13) fight for a loose ball during the St. John’s blowout win over Siena on Nov. 18, 2026, at Carnesecca Arena. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect St. John’s is familiar with the 6-foot-9 Bidunga. The Red Storm faced him in the second round of the NCAA Tournament last March while he was with Kansas . The Red Storm did a strong job in the rebounding department Tuesday against Oregon . They were plus-4 on the boards and limited Oregon big man Malique Ewin to seven points and four rebounds. Prey outplayed him, finishing with 15 points, four rebounds and two assists. The guards rebounded well, as Quinn Ellis, Ian Jackson and Tounde Yessoufou combined for 18 boards. But Louisville is a different animal. The Cardinals will play Bidunga and the 7-foot-2 Ekezie Jr. together at times. The onus will be on the 6-foot-11 Prey to protect the interior. “I feel like it can still get some improvement,” Prey said of his rebounding. “I’m not totally happy with it. But I also am happy with my improvement during the season. I’ve been getting better, and I will continue to improve.” Babacar Sane is still spending more time watching than playing. The athletically gifted forward from Senegal remains a work in progress. Pitino has had a short leash with the 6-foot-7 Sane after turnovers or missed defensive assignments. He was limited to six minutes Tuesday. “I think he’s handling it like a professional,” Jackson said. “He’s been great. Obviously, it’s not the easiest thing to do. He’s approached it well. He’s coming out looking out for ways to get better, looking to understand what he’s doing wrong, looking to fix it. It’s really nice to watch: an older guy being able to handle something like that.”

item.description: As David Bailey builds his case for Defensive Rookie of the Year, Jets coach Aaron Glenn reflected on the team’s decision to select Bailey with the No. 2 overall pick . Take flight with the Jets Text with Brian Costello all season as he brings Sports+ subscribers the latest Jets intel from on the field and off. tRY IT NOW The pick was highly debated at the time, mainly coming down to Bailey and Arvell Reese, who went to the Giants at No. 5. Both players were outstanding prospects, but Glenn said the Jets saw Bailey’s ability to rush the passer as a separator. “I’m a huge believer in, you build a team from the inside out and when you have someone of the magnitude that you know has a chance to affect the game by affecting the quarterback,” Glenn said, “which at the end, if you can affect the quarterback, man, that makes a huge difference in winning and losing. So, that was a huge part of the decision-making of getting a guy that can affect the quarterback and he is a front-line guy. That actually just went into our philosophy in general and I love the pick. I think he’s doing a great job. A lot of things that he can improve on, but that’s the reason why.” David Bailey looks on before the Jets’ loss to the Bills on Nov. 15, 2026 at MetLife Stadium. Getty Images Bailey has played very well for the Jets and has a team-best 9 ½ sacks. He is on the verge of setting the franchise record for sacks by a rookie. Hugh Douglas owns the mark with 10 in 1995. He also has a shot at the NFL rookie record of 14 ½ by Jevon Kearse with the 1999 Titans. Bailey stands out for his play and his style. He does not wear gloves or wristbands and does not celebrate sacks. “I mean, it’s kind of weird when you see it on tape, especially coming out of college because everyone has five towels, everyone has six, seven wristbands on, but I get it,” Glenn said. “Some people say you look good, play good, but I guess that’s what he looks good doing because he damn sure plays good for us. item.title: MLB sues players union to boost lockout as deadline looms
item.description: Major League Baseball sued its players union in New York, hoping to secure protection from antitrust complaints in the wake of a lockout as a deadline looms to sign a new collective bargaining agreement (Mark Brown) Major League Baseball filed a lawsuit against the MLB Players Association on Wednesday seeking legal protection for a lockout expected to begin next week when their current collective bargaining agreement expires. The complaint filed in US District Court in New York seeks a declaration that a lockout would be legal under US antitrust law. The move would safeguard MLB if the players give up union status and try to sue MLB under antitrust law, exposing the league to potentially greater damages. MLB team owners have said they will not accept any new deal without a salary cap, a system the players union has successfully fought for decades. With a Tuesday deadline fast approaching, the lawsuit raised the stakes as both sides fought to determine how to divide billions of dollars in profits. "Today's filing is a defensive measure simply intended to keep the parties at the bargaining table to work towards a new collective bargaining agreement and a full 2027 season," MLB spokesperson Glen Caplin said. "We believe the union is preparing to follow the playbook its new leadership has used against other major professional sports leagues by pretending to 'disclaim' its status as the players' bargaining representative to pursue an antitrust lawsuit as an end run around the bargaining process. "We have asked a federal court in the Southern District of New York to proactively disarm the union's nuclear option of disclaiming." MLBPA interim executive director Bruce Meyer called the lawsuit "completely frivolous" in a statement. "We will respond appropriately, but MLB's decision to run to court in the middle of negotiations rather than bargain in good faith is incredibly disappointing." js/pnb

item.title: Los Angeles Rams vs. Green Bay Packers, Thanksgiving Eve game chat
item.description: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 06: Matthew Stafford #9 of the Los Angeles Rams looks on during a game against the Green Bay Packers at SoFi Stadium on October 06, 2024 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images) | Getty Images Well, the NFL went and found reason to schedule a game on a Wednesday, crowning what’s certain to become it’s own brand of holiday with what’s been dubbed “The Thanksgiving Eve” game. In the early decades of the NFL preceding the 1940s — back when lights on funny looking cars, street lamps, and those indoors were still sometimes powered by oil and kerosene, and a short while later by carbide gas — Wednesday games were not unusual. Since 1940? Before tonight, six NFL games of notoriety were played on a Wednesday in the last 86 years, and none from 1949 through 2011. Do you know when the most recent game was played before this evening’s matchup? September 22, 1948: Los Angeles Rams vs. Detroit Lions (First Wednesday game after 1940) September 5, 2012: Dallas Cowboys vs. New York Giants (Moved from Thursday to avoid President Obama’s DNC speech) December 2, 2020: Baltimore Ravens vs. Pittsburgh Steelers (COVID-19-rescheduled game) December 25, 2024: Kansas City Chiefs vs. Steelers (Christmas Day game) December 25, 2024: Ravens vs. Houston Texans (Christmas Day game) September 9, 2026: Seattle Seahawks vs. New England Patriots (2026 NFL season opener ahead of Thursday game in Australia) Yesterday’s NFL is not today’s NFL, and with each of today’s games put in front of scores of holiday eyes, new interest grows. The move lately has been to put juicy matchups in the best slots of each major holiday. But tonight? This evening, the Los Angeles Rams, Green Bay Packers, and the NFL get a new “holiday” all to themselves. Okay, maybe they’ll have to fight for the attention of people out at informal high school reunions, but you know the game’s going to be on even at Applebee’s. (The impetus for that behemoth’s name is as thrilling as you might guess.) But here we are as a species, soaking in every single second of NFL football available to us. Truth be told, tonight’s game has real potential to be great. Two 6-4 teams are fighting to remain in playoff contention, with Green Bay hanging on to the seventh (and last) seed in the current NFL playoff race. If the regular season ended today, the Rams would be watching the postseason from home as the ninth seed in the NFC. Rooting interests? It’s another NFC-NFC game, so nothing carries too much weight. Additionally, the Bills already played the Rams and will play the Packers Week 14 — that means no real advantage by having one win over other for strength of schedule benefits. Hoping to watch the game? You’ll need a Netflix or NFL+ subscription. Here’s your open thread for the first-ever “Thanksgiving Eve” NFL game. As always, be kind to one another — and in all things, Go Bills!

item.title: Rams versus Packers live discussion: We’re all cheeseheads tonight
item.description: The seventh-seeded Green Bay Packers take on the 9th-seeded Los Angeles Rams. That is not something you would have thought would be true about these two teams at this point in the season if somebody had told you that in August. The Packers hold the tiebreaker over the Rams, thanks to a better conference record. This is a matchup the Packers have dominated. Against the Rams, Green Bay is 20-2 in their last 22 games. They are 10-1 in the last 11. When you own a team to that extent, it’s no longer a trend. It’s domination. Green Bay has fared pretty well in their last dozen contests against the NFC West in general. It’s odd, but it can’t be ignored. The Rams are without Puka Nacua and Davante Adams. That hasn’t slowed down the Rams during the past month, as they still rank sixth in the league in EPA per play and success rate. But they’ve faced the Cardinals twice, the Commanders, Chargers, and Raiders since Week 6. The last time they faced a top offense was in Week 5, and the Bills scored 37 points. To their credit, the Rams have been stingy defensively. Only one team has scored more than 18 points since the Bills game. They’ve dictated much of the game, but this will be an offense that can truly challenge the Rams in ways they haven’t been all season. The Packers are one of those “all-or-nothing” kind of offenses. They can go multiple drives without scoring, and then hit on a big play or three to flip the scoreboard. This should be a lower-scoring game. It probably won’t be fun to watch. History says the Packers will win. Micah Parsons is back, and that should make it a living hell for Matthew Stafford, who has been off all season. Packers 24, Rams 21.

item.title: Royce Lewis Addresses Surprising Trade to Dodgers, Connection to Legend
item.description: Los Angeles Dodgers infielder Royce Lewis arrived via trade Nov. 20 , and spoke about the whirlwind of emotions he felt after the news. Lewis, the No. 1 overall pick in 2017’s draft, had spent his entire professional career with the Twins, and revealed he was “shocked” after the trade. “Shocked is the word,” Lewis said . “I truly thought I was at least going to have one more year to be the first baseman. I was buying in. … I just wanted to produce for (the fans) and win and be a part of the team that helped get them back into a winning state of mind. I felt like we were starting to turn a corner as an org and going in the right direction. I was just excited to be a part of that movement and that turnaround.” While he wanted to be a part of the Twins’ exciting future, Lewis grew up in Southern California and couldn’t be happier to be putting on the Dodgers’ uniform. “We had our morning coffee and (my wife) randomly said, ‘You’re a Dodger,’” Lewis said . “I was like, ‘What the heck is going on’? It’s almost too good to be true. Especially growing up in Southern California, to be on one of the best teams in the league and close to home, is very special to my family. But it hasn’t sunk in yet.” Additionally, Lewis has a special connection with former Dodgers outfielder Matt Kemp, who gave him his “blessing” to wear No. 27 next season. Apr 2, 2026; Kansas City, Missouri, USA; Minnesota Twins third baseman Royce Lewis (23) celebrates after hitting a double during the eighth inning against the Kansas City Royals at Kauffman Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jay Biggerstaff-Imagn Images What is Royce Lewis’ Connection With Matt Kemp? Lewis, as a Southern California native, attended Dodger games regularly in his adolescence, and met Kemp at age 10. Lewis said Kemp is the reason he wanted to pursue baseball, and the former Dodgers fan favorite became a mentor to him during his professional career. Kemp texted Lewis following the trade to congratulate him, and Lewis took the opportunity to ask if he could wear his No. 27 next season. Kemp’s response left little room for interpretation. “Heck yeah. Do it. 100%,” Kemp said, per Lewis on AM 570 LA Sports. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Noel Sanchez (@noisebynoel) Kemp played with the Dodgers for 10 seasons, earning three All-Star nods during those seasons as well as two Gold Glove awards and Silver Slugger awards. He finished second in MVP voting in 2011 with a historic season, finishing second behind Ryan Braun, who later admitted to using performance-enhancing drugs that year. Lewis has some big shoes to fill in the No. 27 jersey next season, and will look to live up to those expectations as the Dodgers push to return to the World Series.

item.title: The Galaxy keep missing the playoffs. Fans want ownership to take action
item.description: Galaxy forward Kyogo Furuhashi reacts during a match against Seattle at Dignity Health Sports Park on Sept. 12. After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. However, general manager Will Kuntz , speaking in a videoconference with the media Friday, agreed things are dismal. “I don’t think we did a good enough job collectively last year,” he said. “So for us, it’s really about taking a hard look at everything we’ve done process-wise and saying ‘hey, how can we be better?’ Because it cannot continue like this.” Galaxy coach Greg Vanney reacts during a match against LAFC at BMO Stadium on Oct. 25. (Luke Hales / Getty Images) Yet Kuntz, the architect of the MLS Cup team, may not be around to see that process through. Vanney still has two years left on his lucrative contract while Kuntz’s deal ends next month, so if there’s going to be a fall guy for the Galaxy’s recent failures, it’s likely to be the GM, not the coach. item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month.
